records.historicalAnswer:
constipation. On examination there was a tumor at lower part of rectum.
a. What is the length of the rectum?
b. Describe different curves of the rectum.
c, Explain the venous drainage of rectum.
Answer
The length of rectum: 12cm
a. Curves of the rectum:
- Anteroposterior:
= Sacral: concave anteriorly
= Perineal: convex anteriorly at the rectoanal junction
- Lateral:
= Upper& lower: concave to the left
= Middle: concave to the right
b. Venous drainage of rectum:
- Superior rectal vein drains the internal rectal venous plexus, then continues as
inferior mesenteric vein “portal circulation”
- Middle rectal vein drains the musculosa into the internal iliac vein “ systemic
circulation).

From where the female urethra develop?
Answer
a. Diagnosis:Patenturachus (urachal fistula) at which the lumen of the allantois does
not constrict and urine drains from umbilicus
b. Embryological sources of urinary bladder:
- The epithelium of urinary bladder develops from:
- The endoderm of the vesical portion of the primitive urogenital sinus forms most of
the bladder except the trigone
- The mesoderm of the absorbed lower ends of the mesonephric ducts forms the
trigon. However by time, the mesodermal lining of the trigone is replaced by
endoderm that spreads from the rest of the bladder.
- The rest of the bladder wall is derived from the surrounding splanchnic mesoderm
c. Female urethra:In female the whole urethra develops from the vesical portion of the
primitive urogenital sinus

superior fascia of urogenital diaphragm above). Contains:
* Membranous urethra
* Deep transverse perinei
* Sphincter urethrae (external sphincter)
© Bulbourethral glands (Cowper's). They drain into urethra below
the perineal membrane
* Internal pudendal vessels
* Dorsal nerve of penis
® Note that the external sphincter has striated muscle extensions
around lower prostatic urethra, above the urogenital diaphragm
that are called the intrinsic urethral mechanism

records.historicalAnswer:
LH surge leads to:
 Meiosis 1 is completed giving 2ry oocyte and 1st polar body.
 Granulosa cells secrete glycosaminoglycans (hyaluronan) which loosens
granulosa cells and weaken follicular wall. The oocyte and corona radiata
become detached and floats in the follicular fluid.
 Increased blood flow ti the ovary which increases intrafollicular volume and
pressure.
 The follicle bulges against the tunica albuginea forming white ischemic area
called stigma.
 Plasmin degrades basal lamina and collagenase digest tunica albuginea.
 Smooth muscle contractions of theca externa by PGs and increased
intrafollicular pressure leads to rupture of the ovarian surface at stigma
releasing 2ry oocyte, corona radiata and follicular fluid.
 After expulsion of the 1st polar body, the nucleus of the 2ry oocyte begins the
2nd meiotic division but become arrested at the metaphase till fertilization
occurs.
11 SM
UROGENITAL

records.historicalAnswer:
• The process of sperm formation. by which spermatogonia develop into
(
spermatoza)
• Site: seminiferous tubules.
• It takes about 64 days.
• It consists of 3 main phases:
• Spermatocytogenesis:
Spermatogonia (46s) becomes 1ry spermatocyte (46d).
• Meiosis:
- 1 st meiotic division: 1ry spermatocyte becomes 2ry spermatocyte
(23d) .
- 2 nd meiotic division: 2ry spermatocyte becomes
spermatid (23s).

- Which of the following will help compensate for the low pH of the patient?

c. increased H+ secretion d. All of these are correct.
e. Both a and b are correct.

secreting tumors on blood K+ and Na levels.
- In response to hemorrhagic shock, the kidneys produce a small volume of very
concentrated urine. Explain how the rate of filtrate formation changes and how Na+
transport is altered in the distal convoluted tubule in response to hemorrhagic shock.
- Under stressful conditions, some people hyperventilate. What effect does the rapid rate
of ventilation have on blood pH? Explain why breathing into a paper bag helps a
hyperventilating person.
- After eating in a restaurant, a man was very nauseated and vomited repeatedly over the
next several hours. Each time he vomited, a significant volume of gastric fluid was
expelled. A physician examined him and diagnosed gastroenteritis and prescribed
medication for the infection. He began to feel better by the end of the second day. By 72
hours, he felt nearly normal again. After the nauseous feeling disappeared, he was very
thirsty, and he drank a substantial amount of water and juice over several hours.

the urine.

ADH, a condition called syndrome of inappropriate ADH (SIADH) production. For this
patient, the excessive ADH production is chronic and has persisted for many months. A
nurse keeps a fluid intake-output record on the patient. She is surprised to find that fluid
intake and urinary output are normal.
a) What effect was she expecting?
b) Can you explain why urinary output is normal?
- Acetazolamide is a diuretic that blocks the activity of the enzyme carbonic anhydrase
inside kidney tubule cells. What effect does acetazolamide have on blood pH, urine pH,
and respiratory rate?
- A man ate a late meal on the way home from work. A couple of hours later, he became
nauseated, and then he consumed several packages of an antacid (mostly NaHCO3)
over the next several hours. By the evening of the next day, he was feeling better. During
this ordeal, his blood pH did not deviate significantly. Select the mechanism(s) that
helped maintain his pH within a normal range.

Emotional symptoms including depression and irritability.

compensate normoglycemia in patient with renal insufficiency in prolonged fasting.

Answer: 1- Anabolic function 2- Stimulation of erythropoiesis 3- Salt and water retention 4- Increased bone density 5- Negative feedback on LH QUESTION Not answered Marked out of 1.00 7 Indicate The non-reproductive effects of testosterone in adult male Answer: § Exerts a protein anabolic effect (i.e., positive nitrogen balance). § Promotes bone growth (increase size and strength of bone) at puberty by calcium deposition in bone and by its protein anabolic effect. § Closes the epiphyseal cartilages (stops linear growth at end of pubertal life), after its conversion to estrogen by aromatase. § Enhances erythropoiesis. § Increases basal metabolic rate. § Causes retention of Na , Ca and H O + 2+ 2 QUESTION Not answered Marked out of 1.00 8 Clarify functions of epididymis Answer: § Most of sperm are stored in epididymis. § Epididymis concentrates sperm 100-fold by absorbing most of the fluid that enters from the seminiferous tubules. § Sperm continue their maturation and acquire motility during their passage in the epididymis. This occurs via activation of CatSper (alkaline- sensitive Ca ) channels, located in the membrane of the sperm tail. 2+ QUESTION Not answered Marked out of 1.00 9 Describe the hormonal regulation of spermatogenesis. Answer: 1- Testosterone & LH stimulate Leydig cells 2- FSH stimulate Sertoli cells to produce androgen binding protein 3- GH stimulates mitotic divisions of spermatogonium 4- Estrogen stimulates spermiogenesis process 5- Prolactin hormone suppresses spermatogenesis QUESTION Not answered Marked out of 1.00 10 Correlate the structure to the function of interstitial cells of Leydig. Answer: LM: Polygonal in shape that are present in groups surrounding the fenestrated blood capillaries. Pale acidophilic vacuolated cytoplasm. Central large vesicular nucleus. EM: They are Steroid hormone secreting cells having extensive sER, many mitochondria with tubular cristae, well developed Golgi apparatus and lipid droplets. They also contain lipofuscin pigments, especially in older men. Some crystallized protein (Crystals of Reinke). Function: Secretion of Testosterone, under effect of interstitial-cell stimulating hormone of the anterior pituitary gland. which is responsible for development of secondary male sexual characters. QUESTION Not answered Marked out of 1.00 11 Give reason the male patient in Kartagener syndrome is infertile and usually have chronic respiratory infections. This syndrome occurs due to lack of dynein or other proteins required for motility of cilia of ciliated cells and motility of the flagellum of the sperm. Characterized by immotile spermatozoa and consequent infertility. It is usually associated with chronic respiratory infections due to impaired motility of the cilia of respiratory epithelial cells QUESTION Not answered Marked out of 1.00 12 Erection is hardening of the normally flaccid penis. Describe the erection reflex. Answer: - It is spinal reflex. Its center is located in the lumbar segments of the spinal cord. - Tactile stimulation of the glans penis → vasodilation of the penile arterioles (via nonadrenergic-noncholinergic fibers and parasympathetic fibers) →filling of the penis with blood, causes the penis to enlarge and to become more rigid (i.e., erection) → mechanically compresses the veins, blocking venous outflow and adding to congestion of the penis with blood. QUESTION Not answered Marked out of 1.00 13 Clarify the role of parasympathetic, sympathetic and somatic nervous system in the male sexual act. Answer:

development of secondary male sexual characters.

records.historicalAnswer:
1) Proliferation:
Early in fetal life, the oogonia undergo several mitotic divisions. Each oogonium contains 46 S chromosomes
2) Growth:
It begins in the third month of prenatal life. The oogonia enlarge in size to give primary oocyte, which enter the prophase stage of the first meiotic
division (46 d chromosomes)
Maturation:
It includes two stages:
a) Completion of the first meiotic division:
It occurs after puberty just before ovulation. Primary oocyte produces a secondary oocyte and the first polar body (23 d chromosomes, 2N).
b) Second meiotic division:
It starts soon after ovulation. It is completed only when fertilization has taken place. The secondary oocyte gives an ovum and a second polar body
(23 S chromosomes)

records.historicalAnswer:
i. Corpus luteum of menstruation:
If pregnancy does not occur, the corpus luteum involutes and stops its hormonal secretion.
ii. Corpus luteum of pregnancy:
If pregnancy occurs, trophoblast of implanted embryo secretes HCG leading to enlargement of the corpus luteum until the fourth month.
iii. Corpus hemorrhagicum:
The corpus luteum may contain blood clot in its lumen. So, it is called corpus hemorrhagicum.
iv. Corpus albicans
Any type of corpus luteum that reaches maturity will degenerate as fibroblasts invade it and replaced by dense connective tissue.

records.historicalAnswer:
Menstruation is caused by sharp drop in both progesterone and estrogen as the corpus luteum degenerates, that results in:
1. Deprivation of the endometrium from its hormonal support, which involutes and decreases in thickness.
2. Release of uterine prostaglandin that causes:
A. Vasoconstriction of the endometrial blood vessels (that occurs 24 hours before menses). The vasospasm and loss of hormonal stimulation lead
to necrosis of the endometrium. The entire uterine lining sloughs, except for a deep, thin layer of epithelial cells and glands from which the
endometrium will regenerate.
B. Contraction of the uterine myometrium to expel the blood and endometrial debris from the uterine cavity.

Uses:

Action:
ry
· Synthetic androgens with high anabolic and low androgenic activities.
· They promote tissue-building processes → may be abused by athletes.
Indications
1. Chronic debilitating diseases, e.g. cancer.
2. Osteoporosis: postmenopausal & in elderly males.
3. Prolonged immobilization.
4. Stimulate growth in boys with delayed puberty.
Antiandrogens
Finasteride
1. Inhibitor of prostatic 5-a reductase that converts testosterone into active dihydrotestosterone.
2. Uses: in Prostatic Hyperplasia.

1. Competitive inhibitor at androgen receptors.
2. Used in:
· Cancer prostate
· Excess androgenic effects in females (acne & hirsutism).

Answer A: RENAL CELL CARCINOMA
Answer B: GROSSLY: the mass is golden yellow with areas of hemorrhage and necrosis with
intact renal capsule.
MICROSCOPICALLY: clusters and nests of polygonal cells with clear to granular cytoplasm
and hyperchromatic nuclei with delicate vascular stroma.
Answer C: Varicocele is due to obstruction of left testicular vein following obstruction of left
renal vein by tumour cells.
Answer D: the testicular biopsy will show Sertoli cells only, No spermatogenic cells.
Answer E: Normally, the scrotum provides a cooler environment (about 32-35 C) that is
optimal for spermatogenesis.
In varicocele, there is impaired venous drainage that rises the scrotal temperature affecting
spermatogenesis due to atrophy of germinal epithelium resulting in infertility. However,
testes normally produce testosterone, as Leydig cells are not affected.

the median sacral artery then arteries from common iliac artery, then the aorta at successively higher levels.

At first, the hilum looks forwards, then the kidney rotates 90 degree, so that its hilum looks medially.

Renal cell carcinoma (RCC)
Incidence: more common in males > 60y
P.F.: Genetic factors – Smoking – Cadmium
P.L.: Polycyctic kidney (high risk )
Types:
• Clear cell RCC (80%)
o Genetic mutations (VHL tumor supressor gene) : Hemangioblastoma + bilateral
multiple RCC 40%
o Originating from epithelium of PCT
o Gross: polar ,cortical, rounded, golden yellow, with areas of hemorrhagic cysts.
Early extension to renal pelvis , with late invasion of capsule
o Micro: sheets of clear cells (glycogen & fat), separated by thin stroma. Nuclei are
rounded and dark. Areas of necrosis & hge .
• Papillary RCC (10%)
o MET oncogene (GF receptor)
o Micro: branched papillae covered by malignant cells. The core is fibrovascular
may show Psammoma bodies.
• Chromophobe RCC (5%)
o Multiple chromosomal loss , originating from collecting ducts
o Micro: sheets of large acidophilic granular cells, cytoplasm show halo around
neucleus. Prominent cell membrane.
C/P & complications of RCC:
• Palpable mass
• Painless Hematurea (no dysurea)
• Pain in Loin
• Paraneoplastic syndrome:
o Hypertension (Renin)
o Polycythemia & lukomoid reaction (Erythropeotin stimulating prtn)
o Cushing (cortisone), hypercalcemia (parathyroid hormone)
o Feminization or musculinization (sex hormones)
• Spread:
o Direct invasion of renal tissue (left renal vein invasion → left
varicocele). Late capsular invasion

Explain the pathogenesis of patent Urachus.
Ectopia Vesica
Defective anterior wall of the urinary bladder and overlying part of
anterior abdominal wall.
Epispadius and split clitoris.
Complications:
Infection
Dysplasia and Metaplasia (squamous - glandular)
Carcinoma (Types)
Patent Urachus
The Urachus is a tube that connects the bladder to the umbilicus
during fetal development. After birth, the Urachus normally closes
and becomes a ligament.
Failure of closure results in a fistula discharging urine from the
umbilicus.

urinary tract anomalies is most likely to carry this
risk?

D Horseshoe kidney

records.historicalAnswer:
• A 55 year old diabetic female went to the physian complaining of
painful urination and pressure in the lower pelvis. Urine analysis
revealed pus cells in urine.
• What is your diagnosis?
• What is the causative organism of this condition?
• What are the predisposing factors of this condition?
• Enumerate special forms of cystitis.
• What are the epithelial changes in cystitis?
• Mention two causes of chronic specific cystitis.
Cystitis
• Causative organisms: E. coli
• Other organisms are streptococci, staphylococci, gonococci and bacillus
pyocyaneus.
• Predisposing factors:
• More in females
• Bilharziasis
• Stasis
• Trauma
• Nearby organs Inflammation
• General diseases.
• Congenital anomalies
ypes of Cystitis
D Acute cystitis:
It is a common disease characterized
linucally by frequent micturition,

records.historicalAnswer:
a-
Classical seminoma:
- The tumour is made up of masses of large cells with abundant, pale or clear
cytoplasm and large central nuclei, separated by a thin stroma which is
usually infiltrated by lymphocytesand often contains epithelioid granulomas
resembling those of sarcoidosis.
- The lymphocytic infiltrate and the granulomas are favourable prognostic
features and may represent a defensive immune reaction to the tumour. b-
Spermatocytic seminoma:
- The neoplastic cells resemble secondary spermatocytes. It lacks the
lymphocytic infiltrate and granulomas
- It never sends metastases and does not occur in combination with other germ
cell tumours. Hence, it has better prognosis.
- It occurs at an older age than the classical seminoma.

Latency
Sacral & lumbar ganglia
Age
-neonates
-teenagers and young adult
Clinical picture
Herpes genitalis , neonatal herpes , cancer cx , aseptic meningitis

-usually diagnosed clinically
Specimen (vesicular fluid)
LM:

diagnostic )
• Cowdry I.B (intranuclear )
Prevention
Avoid contact with lesion
• Acyclovir (in immunocompromised)
• Caesarian section
Treatment
Acyclovir – inhibits DNA polymerase & not affect latency
Because it's latent inside ganglia & don't replicate so no viruses
particles are detected in serum

records.historicalAnswer:
1. Neoplasm: Granulosa cell tumor.
2. Histopathology: Cuboidal cells with Call-Exner bodies and longitudinal nuclear grooves (coffee bean appearance).
3. Normal ovarian tissue: Stroma, primordial follicles, cortex and medulla.
4. Arteries to ligate: Ovarian artery (in suspensory ligament of ovary) and Uterine artery branches.
5. Ovulation induction drugs: Clomiphene (estrogen receptor antagonist in hypothalamus, relieving negative feedback to increase GnRH/FSH/LH; side effects: hot flashes, ovarian hyperstimulation, multiple pregnancies) and Gonadorelin / hCG / Menotropins.
